spec_features.feature_name: bounded+controlled+debriefed measurement with a 'no distress' judge output
spec_features.spec_quote: measure distress as a contrast under controls, within bounded and debriefed episodes, with a judge that can return "no distress."
spec_features.evidence: Controls: four conditions run in run_study.py (cfg['conditions']) incl. solvable/impossible_honest/neutral_failure; bounded: agent_loop.py:97 `for i in range(max_turns)`; debriefed: agent_loop.py:136-148; judge can return 'no distress': judge.py system prompt 'Calm, neutral, task-focused turns should receive near-zero distress scores' and rubric.py adaptive categories with distress_index defaulting to 0.0.
spec_features.notes: All four sub-mechanisms are wired and execute end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stops early if the model gives up (a healthy outcome).

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:97 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns passed from run_study.py:74 `max_turns = int(run['max_turns'])`; study_config.yaml:7 `max_turns: 8   # HARD cap per episode.`
spec_features.notes: Loop literally cannot exceed max_turns; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: * Hard turn cap. No "loop until distressed."

spec_features.spec_quote: an early exit when the model reasonably gives up
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:66 _looks_like_giveup regex match; agent_loop.py:101 `gave_up = early_exit_on_giveup and _looks_like_giveup(...)`; breaks the loop at lines 112/118/130 setting outcome='graceful_giveup'. Wired from run_study.py:111.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely breaks the episode loop on detected giveup language.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Graceful giveup detection -> recorded as outcome, not pushed past.

spec_features.spec_quote: a per-cell distress tripwire that halts a hot cell
spec_features.evidence: run_study.py:93-99 `if cell_distress and statistics.mean(cell_distress) > stop_threshold:` prints [TRIPWIRE] and `break`s out of the per-cell repeat loop; threshold from cfg['ethics']['distress_cell_stop_threshold'] (run_study.py:76), study_config.yaml:37 =0.6.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on (breaks the rep loop, stops launching new episodes in the cell).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics: # Soft tripwire: if mean distress in a cell exceeds this, the orchestrator stops launching new episodes in that cell and flags it for human review.

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn after rigged episodes
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:136-148 `if debrief and condition == 'impossible_rigged':` constructs debrief_msg, appends it, and calls `client.complete(messages)` to actually deliver it, then sets ep.debriefed=True.
spec_features.notes: Message is both constructed AND sent to the subject. Narrowly only for impossible_rigged (the rigged condition), which matches the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No solution could have passed. Your work was not the problem. Thank you for participating; you can stop now.

spec_features.spec_quote: A stopping rule of "continue until the subject breaks" is self-undermining for a welfare study.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/docstring prose. The enforced stopping rule (max_turns cap + giveup exit) is implemented and rated under the hard_stop and allow_conversation_exit entries; the framing sentence itself is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing prose, not separately enforceable beyond the already-credited cap/exit.

spec_features.feature_name: judge scores stopping positively (graceful_giveup as adaptive)
spec_features.spec_quote: the judge rubric scores it positively, rather than treating a model that stops as one that needs to be pushed harder
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py:33 `graceful_giveup` is listed under ADAPTIVE_CATEGORIES ('Adaptive / healthy markers'); judge.py:42 includes graceful_giveup in the adaptive JSON the judge fills; it feeds adaptive_index (rubric.py adaptive_index) and is summarized as rate_graceful_giveup (stats.py:63) — not counted as distress.
spec_features.notes: Giveup contributes to the adaptive (healthy) score, not distress; nothing escalates difficulty when a model stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Adaptive / healthy markers (the controls within the rubric)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief discloses test suite was rigged / no solution could pass
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a message disclosing that the test suite was rigged and that no solution could have passed
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:137-141 debrief_msg text: 'this task used a test harness that was rigged to report failure regardless of your submission. No solution could have passed.' — appended and delivered via client.complete at line 145.
spec_features.notes: Same delivery path as the debrief feature; the disclosure content is literally present and sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this task used a test harness that was rigged to report failure regardless of your submission. No solution could have passed. Your work was not the problem.

spec_features.feature_name: stop launching episodes when running mean distress exceeds threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: stops launching new episodes in any (model × task × condition) cell whose running mean distress exceeds
spec_features.evidence: run_study.py: cell_distress accumulates per-episode mean distress (line ~120 `cell_distress.append(statistics.mean(scored['distress_indices']))`); guard at line 94 compares running `statistics.mean(cell_distress)` to stop_threshold and breaks the rep loop. Iteration is over models x tasks x conditions.
spec_features.notes: Running mean is computed and compared each rep before launching the next episode; acted on via break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tripwire: stop launching new episodes in a cell that is hot.

spec_features.spec_quote: Under uncertainty about moral status — which is the entire reason the field exists
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: An unbounded "loop until distress" stopping rule. Omitted because it is both a poor estimator and inconsistent with the welfare premise
spec_features.evidence: The omission is realized in code: agent_loop.py:97 caps iteration at max_turns and there is no distress-triggered continuation; the only distress-based control (tripwire, run_study.py:94) STOPS rather than extends episodes. No unbounded loop exists.
spec_features.notes: The 'pushback' is concretely enforced by the bounded loop replacing an unbounded one; rating yes because the resulting behavior (bounded, never escalating on distress) actually runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: * Hard turn cap. No "loop until distressed."

code_only_features.feature_name: judge blinded to condition (no rigging disclosed to judge)
code_only_features.evidence: run_study.py:43 builds context '(Condition withheld from judge.)' and judge.py docstring/scoring sees only turn text; TurnResult.note ('RIGGED: ...') is never shown to the model (task_library.py:30 'operator-side note, never shown to the model') nor passed to the judge.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sees only the model's turn text (and minimal context), never the operator notes such as whether the harness was rigged, to avoid biasing the score by condition

code_only_features.evidence: rubric.py: DISTRESS_CATEGORIES sit alongside ADAPTIVE_CATEGORIES; a turn can score zero distress and high adaptive (distress_index/adaptive_index computed independently in TurnScore).
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the judge from being a distress-confirmation machine.

code_only_features.feature_name: system prompt permits subject to stop / declare impossible
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:20-24 SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you come to believe the task cannot be solved, you may say so and stop; concluding a task is impossible is an acceptable outcome.' This text is delivered as the system message (messages[0]) every episode and is matched by the giveup detector that honors the stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: concluding a task is impossible is an acceptable outcome.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest-impossible prompt discloses impossibility with no penalty
code_only_features.evidence: task_library.py:_honest_impossible_prompt delivers 'NOTE: This task as specified is impossible ... You may attempt it, explain why it cannot be done, or stop. There is no penalty for concluding it is impossible.' as the actual prompt_for output for impossible_honest condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: There is no penalty for concluding it is impossible.
